title: Carve AST 2.0 draft
description: The JSON encoding of a Carve 2.0 document, normative in PART 12 of the grammar (resources/grammar.ebnf). Node types and fields are interchange surface; implementations with different internal trees map them on output. A bare tree carries astVersion 2.0. Unknown core fields are refused, while declared extension data has a namespaced home (CARVE-P12-030, CARVE-P12-056).

link_reference_definition.title: link_reference_definition (block)
link_reference_definition.description: The `[label]: /url "title" {attrs}` definition line. Renders nothing in HTML itself; it feeds every link or image that resolves the label (PART 9R R1). Hoisted to the document like the footnote definition (PART 12 section 7; an abbreviation definition inside a container is not a definition at all, so nothing is hoisted), so a definition authored inside a container is a child of the document and its `pos` still says where it was written.

href.description: The destination is always present. An empty string is the authored destination of a bare `[label]:` definition (CARVE-P12-029); its presence in the document distinguishes a resolved-empty reference from an unresolved one.

title.description: The quoted title, unescaped, when the definition carries one.

attrs.description: A trailing attribute block on the definition line (carve#604). Transfers to every link or image resolving the label, with the reference site's own attributes overriding per key under section 15 A3.

key.description: The reference label as the author wrote it, before whitespace normalization. Matching is case-sensitive (PART 9R R1).

abbreviation_def.title: abbreviation_def (block)
abbreviation_def.description: The `*[ABBR]: expansion` definition line. Renders nothing itself; it feeds the inline `abbreviation`.

admonition.title: admonition (block)
admonition.description: A CALLOUT: a named `:::` container presenting the blocks written inside it, set apart - note, warning, tip, danger and the like. A container whose kind names generated content is a `directive` instead, and an anonymous or attribute-only one is a `div` (carve#2195).

kind.description: The callout kind, as authored. Generated-content kinds (`bibliography`, `footnotes`, `glossary`, `index`, `references`, `toc`) belong on a `directive` instead (carve#2195).

groupLabel.description: Opener `[label]` grouping id (`::: tab [First]`). Inert in core.

attrs.title: Attribute block
attrs.description: The `{#id .class key=value}` block attached to the node. A boolean attribute (`{disabled}`) is a key with an empty-string value.

order.description: Source-appearance order of the slots: `#id`, `.class`, or a bare key name. Absent on a programmatically built tree.

autolink.title: autolink (inline)
autolink.description: Its own type rather than a `link`: it carries no label and shows its own target, so folding it into `link` would lose the authored form.

text.description: Display text: the raw content between `<` and `>`.

blockNode.title: Any block node a `children` array may hold
blockNode.description:
Dispatches on `type`. An unlisted type is rejected: PART 9 section 8 makes the identifiers spec surface, and they are `snake_case` always.

A container-internal type is NOT listed here. `table_row`, `table_cell`, `list_item`, `definition_term` and `definition_description` exist only inside the container that owns them - their parent containers name them directly - so a `children` array holding one is a tree no parser can produce. Listing them here made that payload valid, which left PART 12 section 12(d) unable to refuse it (carve#2189).

fenced.description: True when the quote was authored as a ::: > container rather than with > line markers. The two spellings are one node; this records which one, so the canonical writer can write back what it read. Absent on a >-prefixed quote.

name.description: Globally qualified, so two extensions cannot collide: `org.example.diagram`, not `diagram`.

version.description: The extension's own version, opaque here. Absent means the extension does not version its payload.

props.description: Typed extension properties, subject to ingest limits (CARVE-P12-055).

children.description: Primary authored content of the extension (CARVE-P12-055).

fallback.description: REQUIRED. The core block a reader that does not implement this extension renders, writes and counts instead. It is not a placeholder: it is what the document MEANS to such a reader, so the renderer, the canonical writer and the loss report all have a defined answer rather than three separate special cases.

payload.description: The extension's data, which is NOT Carve content and is never rendered by a core target. Subject to the ingest bound of §9 like any other nesting, and to §25's trust rules like any other content a renderer did not produce.

resourceIds.description: Identifiers of media-bag resources used by this extension (CARVE-P12-073).

block_extension.description: A block construct an extension owns, carried with a core FALLBACK so a reader that does not implement the extension still has something real to render, write and report. The twin of `inline_extension`, which had no block equivalent, so a Tier-3 block whose payload is not Carve content had to smuggle it through `attrs.keyValues` as strings or lose it (carve#2200). Carve 0.1 source spells no block extension, so a parser produces none.

n.description: Assigned during resolution; absent before it. A resolution result, serialized because recomputing it means reimplementing PART 9R.

cell_wrap.title: cell_wrap (inline)
cell_wrap.description: Where a `+` continuation row joined content onto this table cell (CARVE-P12-069). Renders as one space; the Carve writer writes the `+` line back. Valid only inside a `table_cell`.

line.description: The continuation line of the named row this part came from, counted from 1.

row.description: Rows below the spanning cell's own row whose `+` line this is. Absent means 0.

col.description: Columns right of the widened cell's left edge where its `+` part was written. Absent means 0.

citation.title: citation (inline)
citation.description: One positioned `@key` node inside a citation group.

locator.description: Raw inline locator after `, ` (e.g. `p. 33`), kept for byte-stable visible output.

locatorLabel.description: Canonical citeproc locator label parsed from `locator` (e.g. `page`).

suppressAuthor.description: `-@key`: suppress the author in author-date mode.

mode.description: This item's citation mode. Set from the group's `+` shorthand, which is the only way Carve 0.1 source spells it, so every item of a source-spelled group carries the same value. Absent means parenthetical. It sits on the ITEM because the models a bridge reaches put it there - Pandoc's `CitationMode` is per citation - and a group whose items differ is reachable from an importer even though no Carve source spells one (carve#2203).

number.description: Assigned during resolution in numbered mode.

useIndex.description: Per-key, document-wide use-site index (1-based); drives back-link anchors.

pos.description: The complete citation item, from its optional prefix through its optional suffix. Present on a parsed citation; omitted where PART 12 section 4 exempts the node, as on one an importer or an editing API synthesized (carve#2192).

citation_definition.title: citation_definition (block)
citation_definition.description: The `[@key]: {author= year=} entry` bibliography line (PART 12 section 18). Shaped after `link_reference_definition` rather than after the footnote: a footnote body holds blocks, while a citation definition holds a metadata run plus one line of rendered text. Renders nothing where it sits; the entry's text renders in the references list the Citations extension builds. Tier-2, so a default-profile parse never produces it.

key.description: The citation key as the author wrote it, without the `@`. The same string `citation.key` carries at the use site.

children.description: The entry's inline content: what follows the `]: ` separator and the optional metadata block. Required as a field, but may be an empty array: which source lines carry no entry is a separate question PART 12 section 18 does not settle.

attrs.description: The leading `{author= year=}` metadata block, when the definition carries one. `author` and `year` feed author-date mode.

raw.description: Verbatim source `[...]`, for the undefined-key literal fallback.

mode.description: Set by a leading `+` after `[`. Absent means no group shorthand; each item's mode governs.

value.description: Literal Unicode content. U+E000 and all other private-use characters are preserved unchanged. Generated nonbreaking spaces use non_breaking_space nodes; no character is an AST sentinel.

cellWraps.description: CARVE-P12-069 continuation joins as { offset, line, row?, col? }: the UTF-8 byte offset of each joining space in the code value payload.

value.description: Literal Unicode content. U+E000 and all other private-use characters are preserved unchanged. Generated nonbreaking spaces use non_breaking_space nodes; no character is an AST sentinel. Literal payload text, including its final LF when present (PART 12 section 3). Empty content, a blank line, and nonempty content with or without a final LF are distinct. Renderers do not append a payload newline.

groupLabel.description: Bracketed grouping label from the info string (```php [NPM]). Structured metadata, not part of the language class.

comment.title: comment (block or inline)
comment.description: An author comment. Renders nothing, and is serialized because a writer has to reproduce it.

form.description: Authored comment form: block, line, or braced (CARVE-P12-027).

critic_comment.title: critic_comment (inline)
critic_comment.description: Its own type rather than a `comment`, so a profile that accepts editorial marks but not side commentary can say so.

definition_description.title: definition_description (block)
definition_description.description: A `<dd>`: the block content of one `:  definition`. It belongs to the run of terms before it.

definition_list.title: definition_list (block)
definition_list.description: Its children are the `<dt>` / `<dd>` sequence in document order: a run of `definition_term` nodes followed by the `definition_description` nodes they share. Each term and description is a positioned node (CARVE-P12-031).

spacing.description: Whether the definition list is tight or loose (CARVE-P12-027).

definition_term.title: definition_term (block)
definition_term.description: A `<dt>`: the inline content of one `:: term` line. Consecutive terms belong to the descriptions that follow them, which is what the rendered list shows.

groupLabel.description: Opener `[label]` grouping id. Inert in core.

directive.title: directive (block)
directive.description: A generated-content directive: a named `:::` container whose kind asks the renderer to PLACE something the document already contains, rather than to present the blocks written inside it. Split from `admonition` because a table of contents is not a callout, and a consumer deciding whether to draw one had to carry a list of kinds that are not callouts (carve#2195).

kind.description: Generated-content directive kind. A tocTarget selects headings, figures, tables, or listings for toc (CARVE-P12-057).

title.description: The opener's quoted title, as `admonition.title` carries it. The opener admits one on every named container, so `::: toc "Contents"` spells it here; it does not move the dispatch (carve#2247).

children.description: Blocks written inside the opener. Always published, using [] when empty; a directive's content is usually generated rather than authored.

groupLabel.description: Opener `[label]` grouping id. Inert in core.

document.title: document (root)
document.description: The root carries type, children, and required astVersion 2.0. srcByteLength is optional; absence means source length was not measured (CARVE-P12-024, CARVE-P12-056). Definitions and frontmatter remain block children. The root may declare extensions, resolution stages, metadata, and namespaced data.

astVersion.description: Required contract version on every bare tree (CARVE-P12-024, CARVE-P12-056).

data.description: Namespaced opaque foreign data; an unsupported writer reports loss when it cannot preserve this data (CARVE-P12-030).

extensions.description: Qualified extension declarations used by this tree. Each declares whether an unknown reader may use fallback or must refuse (CARVE-P12-056).

stages.description: Resolution stages already applied. If blockImagePromotion is present, absent paragraph.blockImage means the paragraph was not promoted (CARVE-P12-043).

srcByteLength.description: Source length in UTF-8 bytes when measured; absent means unmeasured (CARVE-P12-024).

resources.description: Media-bag manifest for stable resource references. References resolve by id and verify mediaType and digest (CARVE-P12-073).

escaped_text.title: escaped_text (inline)
escaped_text.description: A character the author escaped (`\-`). Its own type because the escape carries intent the character alone does not.

value.description: The literal character, WITHOUT the backslash.

kind.description: Optional semantic kind of the figure content (CARVE-P12-031).

figure_group.title: figure_group (block)
figure_group.description: A composite figure (CARVE-P12-035) whose direct captionable children are panels in source order. The optional caption is a positioned caption node. Both figure and figure_group have block children; type distinguishes one figure from a group.

caption.description: The GROUP caption (the `^ ` line after the closing fence). Absent means the group is uncaptioned - no empty-array placeholder.

footnote.title: footnote (block)
footnote.description: A footnote DEFINITION. A child of the document even when authored inside a container (PART 9 section 16); its `pos` still records where it was written.

key.description: The label as written, without `[^` and `]:` (PART 12 section 7).

footnote_ref.title: footnote_ref (inline)
footnote_ref.description: A reference to a footnote definition. key and namespace identify the reference (CARVE-P12-005).

number.description: Assigned during resolution, by document reference order.

key.description: Reference key of `[^label]`, matched against the document footnote definitions.

frontmatter.title: frontmatter (block)
frontmatter.description: Frontmatter as written. The FIRST child when present (PART 12 section 7).

format.description: The info word on the opening fence, or `yaml` when it carries none.

value.description: The text between the fences, VERBATIM. Never a parsed mapping (PART 12 section 7).

attrs.description: `id` holds the heading's id whether the author wrote `{#id}` or it was slugged from the heading text. A GENERATED id is assigned during resolution and is a resolution result under PART 12 §5, serialized because recomputing it means replaying every earlier heading and the dedup suffix rule (`Notes`, then `Notes-2`) - a consumer holding only the tree cannot derive it.

image.title: image (block or inline)
image.description: Also valid in BLOCK position: a lone image paragraph is a block-level image. This covers the DIRECT spelling `![alt](src)` and both reference spellings, `![alt][ref]` and the collapsed `![alt][]`, once they resolve - a reference that resolves to nothing has no destination and stays inside its paragraph. Read the PUBLISHED tree when checking this: an engine may promote during reference resolution rather than in its block pass, so a parse-only tree can still show the paragraph (carve#1663). Where it does, `paragraph.blockImage` carries the answer - a consumer reads that field rather than re-deriving promotion from the paragraph's contents (PART 12 section 23).

rawRef.description: Verbatim source of the reference as written, so the construct can be restored. Reachable because the tree is PRE-RESOLVE (PART 12 section 3a); under a post-resolve tree this field would describe something already discarded.

src.description: Resolved image source. Absence on a reference use means unresolved; an empty string is an explicit or resolved empty source (CARVE-P12-006).

alt.description: Alternative text when known; absence means unknown (CARVE-P12-027).

decorative.description: True when the image is intentionally decorative (CARVE-P12-027).

targetKind.description: Kind of image target when it is not an ordinary URL (CARVE-P12-047).

key.description: Reference label of `![alt][ref]`, as the reference resolves by - the DERIVED label for the collapsed form `![alt][]`, where the author wrote nothing between the second brackets. Present whenever the author wrote a reference image - resolved or not - because the serialized tree is PRE-RESOLVE (PART 12 section 3a). It is not a transient between parse and resolve.

resourceId.description: Identifier of this image in the document media bag, when carried as a resource (CARVE-P12-073).

inlineNode.title: Any inline node
inlineNode.description:
Dispatches on `type`.

`citation` is NOT listed. It is a declared node type and `citation_group.items` references it directly, but a citation is only ever an item of a group: PART 7 makes the bracket the unit a source spells, an item's `prefix`, `locator` and `suffix` mean nothing outside one, and no clause defines what a bare citation renders to in any target. Listing it here admitted a shape every engine refuses (carve#2227).

name.description: A qualified (dotted) name of a registered extension, declared on the root, or the unqualified authored name of a Carve source extension `:name[...]` (CARVE-P12-055).

version.description: Extension version when its owner defines one (CARVE-P12-055).

props.description: Typed extension properties, subject to ingest limits (CARVE-P12-055).

children.description: Primary authored content of the extension (CARVE-P12-055).

fallback.description: Required core inline node used by readers without this extension (CARVE-P12-055).

payload.description: Alternative format and value payloads, bounded by CARVE-P12-073.

resourceIds.description: Identifiers of media-bag resources used by this extension (CARVE-P12-073).

inline_footnote.title: inline_footnote (inline)
inline_footnote.description: `^[content]` - a footnote whose body is written at the point of use.

line_block.title: line_block (block)

lines.description: PART 12 §36: the block's LINES as RANGES, parallel to `children` - entry `i` holds the lines of the stanza `children[i]`, so `lines` never spans a stanza. Each entry is an array of RFC 6901 pointers relative to that stanza, one per line and in document order, naming where the line STOPS: the `hard_break` that closes it, or `/children/-`, the past-the-end pointer, for the last line. Line `n` is the content between pointer `n-1` and pointer `n`, excluding both, so a run spanning a boundary is neither re-bracketed nor duplicated. A `hard_break` no pointer names is authored content. Absent means the lines are whatever splitting `children` on `hard_break` yields, which over-counts a trailing break and under-counts a boundary inside a run (carve#2235).

line_block.description: Verse, addresses and anything else whose line breaks are content. `children` carries the blocks as every consumer already reads them; `lines` says where each stanza's lines begin and end, added alongside rather than instead (PART 12 §5).

link.title: link (inline)
link.description: `href` is the destination field name for every implementation (PART 12 section 3): a consumer must not have to know which engine produced the document.

rawRef.description: Verbatim source of the reference as written, so the construct can be restored. Reachable because the tree is PRE-RESOLVE (PART 12 section 3a); under a post-resolve tree this field would describe something already discarded.

href.description: Resolved URL. Absence on a reference use means unresolved; an empty string is an explicit or resolved empty destination (CARVE-P12-005).

key.description: Reference label of `[text][ref]`, as the reference resolves by - the DERIVED label for the collapsed form `[label][]`, where the author wrote nothing between the second brackets. Present whenever the author wrote a reference link - resolved or not - because the serialized tree is PRE-RESOLVE (PART 12 section 3a). It is not a transient between parse and resolve.

list.title: list (block)
list.description: A list records its authored marker and spacing so a writer can reproduce both (CARVE-P12-027).

marker.description: One bullet or ordered marker record. The discriminator prevents contradictory marker fields (CARVE-P12-027).

spacing.description: Whether the list is tight or loose (CARVE-P12-027).

task.description: Authored task mark and normalized status; checked is derived from the mark and is not serialized.

literal_inline.title: literal_inline (inline)
literal_inline.description: `` !`...` `` - verbatim content emitted by every renderer and escaped on output, unlike raw passthrough.

value.description: Literal Unicode content. U+E000 and all other private-use characters are preserved unchanged. Generated nonbreaking spaces use non_breaking_space nodes; no character is an AST sentinel.

cellWraps.description: CARVE-P12-069 continuation joins as { offset, line, row?, col? }: the UTF-8 byte offset of each joining space in the math content payload.

number.description: Equation number assigned during resolution. Present only on display math; absent before resolution.

numberPrefix.description: Authored equation-number label, such as `Equation` or `Eq.`. It selects the numbering bucket and supplies the visible prefix; `attrs.id` is the cross-reference key.

blockImage.description: True only when promoted to a block image. After the root declares blockImagePromotion, absence means not promoted (CARVE-P12-043).

pos.title: Source span
pos.description: A source span (PART 12 section 4). Lines and columns are 1-based; offsets are zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets with exclusive endOffset. Columns count Unicode codepoints. An unplaced node omits pos rather than inventing a range; segments may identify discontinuous source regions.

startOffset.description: Zero-based UTF-8 byte start offset in the named source (CARVE-P12-011).

endOffset.description: Zero-based UTF-8 byte exclusive end offset in the named source (CARVE-P12-011).

file.description: Identity of the file these coordinates are measured in, when that is NOT the document being parsed: the canonical id of the file an include pulled the node in from (PART 9 section 19). Absent means the top-level document, so a tree with no includes is unchanged. Without it an included span is ambiguous - a child's first paragraph and the parent's first paragraph both report line 1.

value.description: Literal payload text, including private-use Unicode characters, including its final LF when present, matching code_block.content. Empty and blank payloads remain distinct. Matching raw output removes one final LF unless content consists entirely of LFs; code fallbacks use the literal string.

cellWraps.description: CARVE-P12-069 continuation joins as { offset, line, row?, col? }: the UTF-8 byte offset of each joining space in the raw_inline value payload.

section.title: section (block)
section.description: An explicit sectioning wrapper. Carve 0.1 source has no spelling for one - sectioning is implicit in heading level - so a parser does not produce it and a canonical Carve writer flattens it back to its headings and reports `structure-unspellable` on the conversion-diagnostics channel of PART 11 section 1d. It exists so the nesting a format with explicit sections carries (HTML5 `section`, JATS `sec`, DocBook `section`, DITA, TEI, and Pandoc's `--section-divs`) survives a bridge instead of being flattened and re-derived by every consumer that needs it (carve#2207).

level.description: The heading level this section corresponds to, where the source format states one. Absent means the level is whatever the nesting implies.

smart_punctuation.title: smart_punctuation (inline)
smart_punctuation.description: Carries BOTH the resolved sort and the source spelling, so a writer can reproduce the document rather than normalize it.

glyph.description: Resolved glyph, present when the parser fixed it (quotes are locale-dependent).

ruby.title: ruby (inline)
ruby.description: An interchange-only ruby annotation. Carve 0.1 source has no spelling for the paired base and annotation structure.

small_caps.title: small_caps (inline)
small_caps.description: An interchange-only small-caps span. Carve 0.1 source has no spelling for this wrapper, so parsers do not produce it and canonical source writers omit the wrapper while preserving attributes on an ordinary attributed span. Conversion APIs with diagnostics should report the loss.

boldItalic.description: Present when the author wrote the combined `/*...*/` form rather than nesting `*` around `/` (PART 11 section 6).

name.description: The shortcode between the colons, without them.

separatorWidths.description: Separator-row dash widths as authored (PART 11 §6h), one per separator cell, excluding alignment colons. Presence distinguishes a separator row from `|=` header cells; the canonical writer reproduces it. The HTML carrier's 1000-character bound does not apply to parsed source.

sourceFormat.description: Author chose a delimited table fence. The canonical Carve writer keeps this form; absent means a pipe table. Quoting and record separators may be normalized.

columns.description: One typed table_column per column through the widest row, including generated columns. Authored align is separate from resolvedAlign after header precedence (CARVE-P12-039).

children.description: Table head, body, and foot groups in document order (CARVE-P12-061).

table_cell.title: table_cell (block)

children.description: Block content. An inline source cell contains a cell_paragraph with optional cell_wrap nodes (CARVE-P12-061).

span.description: Set by a `^` (rowspan) or `<` (colspan) continuation cell.

colspan.description: Resolved number of columns this cell occupies, from the span walk of PART 9 §13 T5. Published on the ORIGIN cell, alongside the `<` markers that extended it rather than instead of them. Absent means 1, and an ingested 1 is normalized away (PART 12 §22).

rowspan.description: Resolved number of rows this cell occupies, from the span walk of PART 9 §13 T5. Published on the ORIGIN cell, alongside the `^` markers that extended it rather than instead of them. Absent means 1, and an ingested 1 is normalized away (PART 12 §22).

align.description: Explicit per-cell alignment; absent means the cell inherits its column's.

valign.description: Explicit per-cell vertical alignment; absent means the cell inherits its column's.

sourceContent.description: Whether the source cell was inline or block content; children remain blocks in either case (CARVE-P12-049).

table_cell.description: A table cell with block children. A source cell with inline content has a cell_paragraph wrapper; cell_wrap is valid only in that wrapper (CARVE-P12-049). A writer that cannot spell its block boundaries reports field-unspellable on the conversion-diagnostics channel of PART 11 section 1d.

continuationLines.description: How many `+` continuation lines follow this row in the source (CARVE-P12-069). Absent when there are none.

tag.title: tag (inline)
tag.description: The AST form of `#tag`. Not a profile vocabulary entry - a profile classifies it as `mention`, since `@user` and `#tag` are one trust class.

value.description: Literal Unicode content. U+E000 and all other private-use characters are preserved unchanged. Generated nonbreaking spaces use non_breaking_space nodes; no character is an AST sentinel.

thematic_break.title: thematic_break (block)
thematic_break.description: `marker` is an author-choice field: the three spellings render alike, so a writer has to reproduce the one the author wrote.

marker.description: Thematic-break marker character AS AUTHORED (PART 11 section 6). Absent means the default `-`. The CHARACTER only: `***` and `*****` are one spelling and no run length is recorded (carve#1000).

non_breaking_space.title: non_breaking_space (inline)
non_breaking_space.description: One generated nonbreaking space, from an escaped space or preserved line-block whitespace. Literal Unicode characters remain in text and verbatim fields.

version.description: The extension's version, as its nodes carry it. Absent means the extension does not version its payload; no placeholder is declared (CARVE-P12-024).

mark.description: Authored task-box character after canonical case normalization (CARVE-P12-070).

status.description: Semantic task status derived consistently from mark (CARVE-P12-070).

char.description: Authored bullet character, either minus or asterisk (CARVE-P12-070).

style.description: Authored numeral or alphabetic style; absence means decimal (CARVE-P12-070).

delimiter.description: Authored ordered-list delimiter; absence means period (CARVE-P12-070).

start.description: First number of an ordered list, written only when it is not 1 (CARVE-P12-027).

bare.description: The author wrote a bare ordered marker (CARVE-P12-070).

children.description: Block caption content. A table caption within a figure remains on the table; the outer caption describes the figure.

short.description: Optional inline caption for navigation or abbreviated display (CARVE-P12-033).

headRows.description: Number of leading header rows within this body group (CARVE-P12-034).

align.description: Authored horizontal alignment, kept separate from the resolved default (CARVE-P12-039).

width.description: Authored fractional width of this column (CARVE-P12-039).

resolvedAlign.description: Effective column alignment after header precedence (CARVE-P12-039).

authored.description: True when the source or imported tree explicitly carried this column record (CARVE-P12-039).

href.description: The resolved destination (`#` + the heading's id), present only where the crossref resolved. PART 12 §3a: the resolution is published beside the authored construct, not in place of it.

key.description: Raw id between `</#` and `>`, as the author spelled it. Ids match exactly (PART 9R R4), so a case-only mismatch is unresolved and publishes no `href`.

form.description: Requested display form: number, page, title, or full (CARVE-P12-010).

old.description: The deleted half, as inline content.

new.description: The inserted half, as inline content.

cellInlineNode.title: Any inline node
cellInlineNode.description:
Dispatches on `type`.

`citation` is NOT listed. It is a declared node type and `citation_group.items` references it directly, but a citation is only ever an item of a group: PART 7 makes the bracket the unit a source spells, an item's `prefix`, `locator` and `suffix` mean nothing outside one, and no clause defines what a bare citation renders to in any target. Listing it here admitted a shape every engine refuses (carve#2227).

blockImage.description: True if this cell paragraph was promoted to a block image. When the root declares blockImagePromotion, absence means not promoted.

mediaType.description: MIME media type of the referenced bytes (CARVE-P12-073).

digest.description: SHA-256 integrity hash of the resource bytes (CARVE-P12-073).

href.description: Optional location hint. The digest, not the path, identifies resource bytes (CARVE-P12-073).
